library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

```{r load-model}
mod <- readModelDb("Haynes_2026_cephalexin")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r ui$reference`
* Description: `r ui$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1093/ofid/ofag611>

Cephalexin is an oral first-generation cephalosporin used both as initial
therapy and as oral transition therapy for systemic methicillin-susceptible
*Staphylococcus aureus* (MSSA) and Enterobacterales infections. Haynes 2026
pooled four cephalexin PK datasets spanning preterm-born young infants to young
adults into one population PK model, then used it to compute the probability
of target attainment (PTA) for free-drug time above the MIC (fT>MIC) targets
across the age range.

The final model is a one-compartment model with first-order absorption, an
absorption lag time and linear elimination. All doses were enteral, so volume
and clearance are apparent (`Vd/F`, `CL/F`). Both scale with fat-free mass
(FFM) by estimated power exponents around a 56 kg reference; `CL/F` matures
with postmenstrual age (PMA) through a sigmoid Hill function, and the
absorption rate constant is lowered by a fixed scalar in infants up to 21 days
old.

The neonatal study in this pool (Study 1) was also modelled on its own in
`Haynes_2025_cephalexin`, which uses total body weight and a power function of
PMA. The two models are separate analyses and both are packaged.

# Population

Seventy-one subjects contributed 360 cephalexin plasma concentrations (Haynes
2026 Table 1): 33 hospitalized young infants aged 9-56 days at Children's
Hospital Colorado (Study 1, gestational age at birth 29 3/7 to 40 6/7 weeks),
15 children aged 0.82-17.8 years with musculoskeletal infections at the same
hospital (Study 2), 12 children aged 1.2-16.7 years with musculoskeletal
infections in Montreal sampled at steady state (Study 3), and 11 healthy adults
aged 18-29 years in New Zealand given a single 1000 mg dose after a meal
(Study 4). Overall median age was 1.46 years, median body weight 10.95 kg
(range 2.2-112), median FFM 8.06 kg (range 1.99-77.18), and 39% were female.
Doses ranged from 8.93 to 51.18 mg/kg (28.5-1500 mg). Twenty-two samples (6%)
were below the limit of quantification and were handled with the M4
likelihood.

```{r population}
str(ui$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source. The
table collects them.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| One compartment, first-order absorption with lag, linear elimination | structure | Results "Final Model"; Supplementary Appendix C |
| `Tlag = Tlag_pop * exp(eta)` | equation | Supplementary Appendix C |
| `Ka = Ka_pop * exp(beta_PNA) * exp(eta)` for PNA <= 21 days, else `Ka_pop * exp(eta)` | equation | Supplementary Appendix C |
| `Vd/F = Vd_pop/F * (FFM/56)^0.92` | equation | Supplementary Appendix C |
| `CL/F = CL_pop/F * (FFM/56)^0.82 * PMA^5.06 / (42.96^5.06 + PMA^5.06) * exp(eta)` | equation | Supplementary Appendix C |
| `ltlag` | 0.53 h (RSE 13.16%) | Table 2 'Tlag (h)' |
| `lka` | 1.59 1/h (RSE 18.2%) | Table 2 'Ka (1/h)' |
| `e_pnale21d_ka` | -0.81 (RSE 34.23%) | Table 2 'beta age < 21d_Ka' |
| `lvc` | 22.04 L/56 kg FFM (RSE 7.57%) | Table 2 'Vd/F (L/56 kg)' |
| `e_ffm_vc` | 0.92 (RSE 2.7%) | Table 2 'beta FFM_V' |
| `lcl` | 16.6 L/h/56 kg FFM (RSE 4.25%) | Table 2 'CL/F (L/h/56 kg)' |
| `e_ffm_cl` | 0.82 (RSE 2.82%) | Table 2 'beta FFM_CL' |
| `lhill_mat` | 5.06 (RSE 15.51%) | Table 2 'Hill coefficient' |
| `ltmat50` | 42.96 weeks PMA (RSE 2.08%) | Table 2 'TM50 (weeks PMA)' |
| `etaltlag` | CV 87.13% -> variance 0.56484 | Table 2 'IIV for Tlag (CV%)' |
| `etalka` | CV 51.87% -> variance 0.23827 | Table 2 'IIV for Ka (CV%)' |
| `etalcl` | CV 17.25% -> variance 0.029322 | Table 2 'IIV for CL/F (CV%)' |
| No IIV on Vd/F | fixed to 0 | Results "Final Model"; Appendix C (53.8% shrinkage) |
| `addSd` | 0.31 mg/L (RSE 18.01%) | Table 2 'Constant (a, mg/L)' |
| `propSd` | 0.21 (RSE 9.39%) | Table 2 'Proportional (b)' |
| Protein binding (simulations only) | 10% | Methods "Outcomes" |
| Gestational age of children and adults | 40 weeks (so PMA = 40 + postnatal weeks) | Supplementary Appendix A |

## Random-effect scale: CV to variance

Table 2 reports the random effects as CV%. For a log-normal parameter Monolix
reports `CV = sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1)`, so the variance is `log(1 + CV^2)`. The
bootstrap medians printed in the same rows (0.77, 0.45, 0.16) are on the omega
(SD) scale and agree with the converted values, which confirms the reading.

```{r omega-scale}
cv <- c(Tlag = 0.8713, Ka = 0.5187, `CL/F` = 0.1725)
om <- ui$omega
omega_chk <- data.frame(
  Parameter = names(cv),
  `Table 2 CV (%)` = 100 * cv,
  `Model variance` = diag(om)[c("etaltlag", "etalka", "etalcl")],
  `Model CV (%)` = 100 * sqrt(exp(diag(om)[c("etaltlag", "etalka", "etalcl")]) - 1),
  `Model omega (SD)` = sqrt(diag(om)[c("etaltlag", "etalka", "etalcl")]),
  `Bootstrap median omega` = c(0.77, 0.45, 0.16),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(omega_chk, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)

# Pure arithmetic: the converted variances must return the printed CVs.
stopifnot(max(abs(omega_chk$`Model CV (%)` - omega_chk$`Table 2 CV (%)`)) < 0.01)
# The bootstrap medians differ from the point estimates by bootstrap noise only.
stopifnot(max(abs(omega_chk$`Model omega (SD)` - omega_chk$`Bootstrap median omega`)) < 0.05)
```

# Covariate model verification

Individual parameters are read back from typical-value solves. Event tables
carry observation rows on `central` so every subject's covariates are used.

```{r param-helper}
param_events <- function(d) {
  bind_rows(
    d |> mutate(time = 0, amt = 1, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
    d |>
      tidyr::crossing(time = c(0, 1)) |>
      mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
    select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, dplyr::everything())
}
# A typical-value model has no omega, so rxode2 warns on every multi-subject
# solve; that is intended here, so muffle that one warning only.
muffle_no_omega <- function(w) {
  if (grepl("multi-subject simulation without", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
}
read_params <- function(d, keep) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, param_events(d), keep = keep),
    warning = muffle_no_omega
  ) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    group_by(id) |>
    slice(1) |>
    ungroup()
}
```

At 56 kg FFM, an adult PMA (where the Hill term is essentially 1) and a
postnatal age above 21 days, the model must return the Table 2 typical values.
The Hill term must be exactly one half at PMA = TM50, and the 21-day cut must
scale ka by `exp(-0.81)`.

```{r reference-checks}
ref <- data.frame(
  id = 1:4,
  FFM = 56,
  PAGE = c(40 + 25 * 52.1775, 42.96, 40 + 25 * 52.1775, 40 + 25 * 52.1775),
  PNA = c(25 * 12, 0.2, 20.5 / 30.4375, 21.5 / 30.4375)
)
ref_par <- read_params(ref, keep = c("FFM", "PAGE", "PNA"))
stopifnot(nrow(ref_par) == 4L, !anyNA(ref_par$cl))

ref_tab <- data.frame(
  Quantity = c("Tlag (h)", "Ka (1/h)", "Vd/F (L)", "CL/F (L/h)",
               "Hill term at PMA = TM50", "ka(PNA 20.5 d) / ka(PNA 21.5 d)"),
  Model = c(ref_par$tlag[1], ref_par$ka[1], ref_par$vc[1], ref_par$cl[1],
            ref_par$fmat[2], ref_par$ka[3] / ref_par$ka[4]),
  Expected = c(0.53, 1.59, 22.04, 16.6, 0.5, exp(-0.81))
)
ref_tab$`Diff (%)` <- 100 * (ref_tab$Model - ref_tab$Expected) / ref_tab$Expected
knitr::kable(ref_tab, digits = 5)

# Deterministic. CL/F at a 25-year-old's PMA (1344 weeks) carries a Hill term
# of 1 - (42.96 / 1344)^5.06 = 1 - 2.7e-8, i.e. 2.7e-6 percent below the
# Table 2 value; every other row is exact to floating point.
stopifnot(max(abs(ref_tab$`Diff (%)`)) < 1e-4)
```

## Clearance maturation (replicates the population curve of Figure S3)

Figure S3 plots individual CL as a percentage of the adult value against PMA,
with the population Hill curve. The curve below is the packaged model's
maturation term.

```{r maturation-figure, fig.cap = "Population maturation of cephalexin CL/F with postmenstrual age (replicates the solid line of Haynes 2026 Figure S3). Dashed line: TM50 = 42.96 weeks."}
mat_grid <- data.frame(id = 1:200, PAGE = exp(seq(log(28), log(300), length.out = 200))) |>
  mutate(FFM = 56, PNA = 12)
mat_par <- read_params(mat_grid, keep = c("PAGE"))
stopifnot(nrow(mat_par) == 200L, all(diff(mat_par$fmat) > 0))

ggplot(mat_par, aes(PAGE, 100 * fmat)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 42.96, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Postmenstrual age (weeks)", y = "CL/F (% of adult value)") +
  theme_bw()
```

# Typical values at each study's median covariates

The Discussion compares the model's clearance with each source study's
published estimate: Study 1 0.67 L/h, Study 2 11.8 L/h, Study 3 0.263 L/h/kg
and Study 4 14.8 L/h. Supplementary Table S2 gives the median individual
estimates by age group. The table below evaluates the **typical** model at each
study's Table 1 median FFM, age and gestational age. A typical value at the
median covariates is not the same statistic as the median of the individual
estimates, so close but not exact agreement is expected.

```{r study-medians}
studies <- data.frame(
  id = 1:4,
  Study = c("1: young infants", "2: CHCO children", "3: Montreal children", "4: young adults"),
  FFM = c(2.99, 36.46, 21.06, 48.97),
  WT = c(3.35, 51.8, 25, 75),
  ga_wk = c(37 + 2 / 7, 40, 40, 40),
  age_d = c(31.2, 12.22 * 365.25, 7.61 * 365.25, 20.42 * 365.25)
) |>
  mutate(PNA = age_d / 30.4375, PAGE = ga_wk + age_d / 7)

st_par <- read_params(studies, keep = c("Study", "FFM", "WT", "PAGE"))
stopifnot(nrow(st_par) == 4L)

st_tab <- st_par |>
  transmute(
    Study,
    `FFM (kg)` = FFM, `PMA (wk)` = PAGE,
    `Model CL/F (L/h)` = cl,
    `Model CL/F per kg (L/h/kg)` = cl / WT,
    `Model Vd/F (L)` = vc,
    `Model t1/2 (h)` = log(2) * vc / cl,
    `Discussion CL` = c("0.67 L/h", "11.8 L/h", "0.263 L/h/kg", "14.8 L/h"),
    model_cmp = c(cl[1], cl[2], cl[3] / WT[3], cl[4]),
    published = c(0.67, 11.8, 0.263, 14.8),
    `Diff (%)` = 100 * (model_cmp - published) / published
  )
knitr::kable(st_tab |> select(-model_cmp, -published), digits = 3)

# Deterministic. Realised differences are +3.9%, -1.1%, +13.2% and +0.5%.
# Study 3's comparison is a per-kg clearance, where the typical value at the
# median FFM divided by the median weight is a different statistic from the
# median of individual CL/kg; the other three studies agree within 4%.
stopifnot(max(abs(st_tab$`Diff (%)`[c(1, 2, 4)])) < 5)
stopifnot(abs(st_tab$`Diff (%)`[3]) < 20)
```

The adult (Study 4) typical half-life of about 0.9 h and volume of about 19.5 L
match the Table S2 18-30 year medians (0.897 h, 19.5 L). The Study 1 typical
infant (1.48 h, 1.49 L) sits between the Table S2 medians for 7-28 days
(1.81 h, 1.39 L) and 29 days to < 2 years (1.37 h, 1.69 L), as expected for a
cohort whose median postnatal age is 31 days.

# Virtual cohorts

The paper simulated 11 age groups of 5000 subjects generated in PK-Sim from
NHANES and neonatal distributions, which are not published. Two groups are
reconstructed here at 200 subjects each, the cap for these vignettes:

* **Young adults, 18-30 years.** Sex 50/50; height normal (176 +/- 7.5 cm male,
  162 +/- 7 cm female); weight log-normal (median 80 kg male, 68 kg female, CV
  about 20%), approximating NHANES young adults. FFM from the Janmahasatian
  2005 equation, which Supplementary Appendix A names for adults.
* **Young infants, 7 to < 60 days.** Gestational age uniform over 30-41 weeks
  and postnatal age uniform over 7-60 days, the strata of the paper's infant
  groups. Weight from an approximate 50th-percentile birth weight for
  gestational age, a 5% early weight loss and 25 g/day growth, with 12% CV.
  FFM is taken as 0.893 x weight, the ratio of the Study 1 median FFM to median
  weight in Table 1 (2.99 / 3.35), because the paper's infant FFM equation
  (O'Hanlon 2023) needs sex-specific maturation constants it does not print.

```{r cohort}
n_per_arm <- 200L

set.seed(2026001)
male <- rep(c(1, 0), length.out = n_per_arm)
ht <- ifelse(male == 1, stats::rnorm(n_per_arm, 176, 7.5), stats::rnorm(n_per_arm, 162, 7))
wt <- ifelse(male == 1, 80, 68) * stats::rlnorm(n_per_arm, 0, 0.2)
bmi <- wt / (ht / 100)^2
adults <- data.frame(
  grp = "Adults 18-30 y",
  age_d = stats::runif(n_per_arm, 18, 30) * 365.25,
  ga_wk = 40, WT = wt,
  FFM = ifelse(male == 1, 9270 * wt / (6680 + 216 * bmi), 9270 * wt / (8780 + 244 * bmi))
)

bw_knots <- data.frame(GA = c(30, 32, 34, 36, 38, 40, 41), BW = c(1.4, 1.8, 2.3, 2.8, 3.2, 3.5, 3.6))
set.seed(2026002)
ga <- stats::runif(n_per_arm, 30, 41)
pna_d <- stats::runif(n_per_arm, 7, 60)
wt_inf <- (stats::approx(bw_knots$GA, bw_knots$BW, xout = ga)$y * 0.95 + 0.025 * (pna_d - 7)) *
  stats::rlnorm(n_per_arm, 0, 0.12)
infants <- data.frame(
  grp = "Infants 7-<60 d",
  age_d = pna_d, ga_wk = ga, WT = wt_inf, FFM = 0.893 * wt_inf
)

cohort <- bind_rows(adults, infants) |>
  mutate(
    id = dplyr::row_number(),
    PNA = age_d / 30.4375,
    PAGE = ga_wk + age_d / 7
  )

cohort |>
  group_by(grp) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    `WT (kg)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f-%.1f)", median(WT), min(WT), max(WT)),
    `FFM (kg)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f-%.1f)", median(FFM), min(FFM), max(FFM)),
    `PMA (wk)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f-%.1f)", median(PAGE), min(PAGE), max(PAGE)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Reconstructed virtual cohorts, median (range).")

stopifnot(nrow(cohort) == 2L * n_per_arm)
# The adult FFM median should sit near the Study 4 median of 48.97 kg, and the
# infant FFM inside the Study 1 range of 1.99-4.17 kg at the centre.
stopifnot(abs(median(cohort$FFM[cohort$grp == "Adults 18-30 y"]) - 49) < 6)
stopifnot(median(cohort$FFM[cohort$grp == "Infants 7-<60 d"]) > 2,
          median(cohort$FFM[cohort$grp == "Infants 7-<60 d"]) < 4.2)
```

# Single-dose simulation and PKNCA

Adults receive 1000 mg (the Study 4 dose and the paper's adult AUC-matching
reference) and infants 25 mg/kg, with full inter-individual variability.

```{r single-dose-sim}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026101)
sd_grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.05), seq(2.25, 8, by = 0.25), seq(9, 16, by = 1))))

cohort_sd <- cohort |> mutate(dose_mg = ifelse(grp == "Adults 18-30 y", 1000, 25 * WT))
ev_sd <- bind_rows(
  cohort_sd |> mutate(time = 0, amt = dose_mg, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
  cohort_sd |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = sd_grid) |>
    mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, FFM, PNA, PAGE, grp, dose_mg)

sim_sd <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_sd, keep = c("grp", "dose_mg")) |>
  as.data.frame()
stopifnot(all(is.finite(sim_sd$Cc)), all(sim_sd$Cc >= 0))
```

```{r single-dose-figure, fig.cap = "Simulated cephalexin plasma concentrations after a single oral dose (adults 1000 mg; infants 25 mg/kg). Line = median, band = 5th-95th percentile."}
sim_sd |>
  group_by(grp, time) |>
  summarise(med = median(Cc), lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, med, ymin = lo, ymax = hi, fill = grp, colour = grp)) +
  geom_ribbon(alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Cephalexin concentration (mg/L)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r pknca}
nca_in <- sim_sd |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, grp, dose_mg)
nca_in <- bind_rows(
  nca_in,
  nca_in |> distinct(id, grp, dose_mg) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, grp, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, time)
dose_in <- nca_in |> distinct(id, grp, dose_mg) |> mutate(time = 0)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(
  PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_in, Cc ~ time | grp + id),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_in, dose_mg ~ time | grp + id),
    intervals = data.frame(
      start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
      aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
    )
  ),
  verbose = FALSE
)
nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  select(id, grp, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
stopifnot(nrow(nca_wide) == nrow(cohort))

nca_wide |>
  group_by(grp) |>
  summarise(
    `Cmax (mg/L)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", median(cmax), quantile(cmax, 0.05), quantile(cmax, 0.95)),
    `Tmax (h)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", median(tmax), quantile(tmax, 0.05), quantile(tmax, 0.95)),
    `AUCinf (mg*h/L)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f-%.1f)", median(aucinf.obs, na.rm = TRUE),
                                quantile(aucinf.obs, 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), quantile(aucinf.obs, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE)),
    `t1/2 (h)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", median(half.life, na.rm = TRUE),
                         quantile(half.life, 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), quantile(half.life, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated single-dose NCA, median (5th-95th percentile).")
```

## Comparison with the published adult exposure

The Results "AUC Matching" section reports a median AUC0-inf of 65.9 mg*h/L for
the paper's virtual young adults after 1000 mg, against 68.1 mg*h/L from the
Study 4 NCA and 67.46 mg*h/L from the 13 literature values of Table S1. Table
S2 gives an adult median half-life of 0.897 h.

```{r nca-compare}
adult_nca <- nca_wide |> filter(grp == "Adults 18-30 y")
sim_tab <- data.frame(
  Group = "Adults 18-30 y, 1000 mg",
  aucinf.obs = median(adult_nca$aucinf.obs, na.rm = TRUE),
  half.life = median(adult_nca$half.life, na.rm = TRUE)
)
ref_tab <- data.frame(Group = "Adults 18-30 y, 1000 mg", aucinf.obs = 65.9, half.life = 0.897)
nca_cmp <- ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_tab,
  reference = ref_tab,
  by = "Group",
  units = c(aucinf.obs = "mg*h/L", half.life = "h"),
  label_first_column = "NCA parameter"
)
knitr::kable(
  nca_cmp,
  caption = "Simulated vs published adult exposure (AUC0-inf: Results 'AUC Matching'; t1/2: Table S2 median)."
)
attr(nca_cmp, "footnote")

# Centre-of-distribution checks. A wrong clearance, FFM exponent or unit
# shifts AUC by tens of percent; the reconstructed NHANES cohort moves it by a
# few percent at most.
stopifnot(abs(sim_tab$aucinf.obs / 65.9 - 1) < 0.12)
stopifnot(abs(sim_tab$half.life / 0.897 - 1) < 0.12)
```

# Probability of target attainment (Supplementary Table S3)

PTA is the fraction of subjects whose free concentration (10% protein binding,
Methods "Outcomes") exceeds the MIC for at least the target percentage of the
24-48 h interval after the first dose. The three regimens of Table S3 are
simulated for both cohorts, with doses capped as in the paper: 25 mg/kg (max
1000 mg) every 8 h, 25 mg/kg (max 1000 mg) every 6 h and 37.5 mg/kg (max
1500 mg) every 6 h. Adults therefore receive 1000 mg, 1000 mg and 1500 mg.

```{r pta-sim}
regimens <- data.frame(
  regimen = c("25 mg/kg q8h", "25 mg/kg q6h", "37.5 mg/kg q6h"),
  mgkg = c(25, 25, 37.5), cap = c(1000, 1000, 1500), tau = c(8, 6, 6)
)
pta_cohort <- tidyr::crossing(cohort |> select(-id), regimens) |>
  mutate(id = dplyr::row_number(), amt = pmin(mgkg * WT, cap))

obs_grid <- seq(24, 47.95, by = 0.05)
ev_pta <- bind_rows(
  pta_cohort |>
    group_by(id) |>
    reframe(time = seq(0, 47.999, by = tau[1]), amt = amt[1]) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
  pta_cohort |>
    select(id) |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = obs_grid) |>
    mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  left_join(pta_cohort |> select(id, FFM, PNA, PAGE, grp, regimen), by = "id") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026201)
sim_pta <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_pta, keep = c("grp", "regimen")) |>
  as.data.frame()
stopifnot(nrow(sim_pta) == nrow(pta_cohort) * length(obs_grid))

fu <- 0.9
mics <- c(1, 2, 4, 8, 16)
ft <- tidyr::crossing(sim_pta |> select(id, grp, regimen, Cc), mic = mics) |>
  group_by(id, grp, regimen, mic) |>
  summarise(ftmic = mean(fu * Cc > mic), .groups = "drop")
targets <- c(0.25, 0.35, 0.40, 0.50, 0.60)
pta <- tidyr::crossing(ft, target = targets) |>
  group_by(grp, regimen, mic, target) |>
  summarise(pta = 100 * mean(ftmic >= target), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r pta-figure, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 7, fig.cap = "PTA against MIC. Lines: simulated with the packaged model; points: Supplementary Table S3 (the same regimens and age groups as Figure 2 of Haynes 2026)."}
ggplot(pta_cmp, aes(mic, pta, colour = factor(100 * target))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(aes(y = pta_pub), shape = 1, size = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 90, linetype = "dotted", colour = "red") +
  facet_grid(regimen ~ grp) +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = "log2", breaks = mics) +
  labs(x = "MIC (mg/L)", y = "PTA (%)", colour = "fT>MIC target (%)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Adult PTAs track Table S3 to within a few points in every cell. For infants,
the cells at MIC 16 mg/L with the stricter targets run up to about 15 points
below Table S3. Those cells sit on the steep part of the PTA curve, where the
answer depends on the share of the youngest, most preterm infants in the
cohort; the paper's PK-Sim infant population is not published, so the
reconstructed cohort's age mix is the most likely source.

```{r pta-table}
pta_cmp |>
  filter(mic %in% c(8, 16)) |>
  arrange(grp, regimen, target, mic) |>
  transmute(
    `Age group` = grp, Regimen = regimen,
    `Target (% fT>MIC)` = 100 * target, `MIC (mg/L)` = mic,
    `Simulated PTA (%)` = round(pta), `Table S3 PTA (%)` = pta_pub,
    `Difference (points)` = round(diff)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "PTA at the discriminating MICs (8 and 16 mg/L).")

pta_summary <- pta_cmp |>
  group_by(grp) |>
  summarise(
    `Median abs diff (points)` = median(abs(diff)),
    `90th pct abs diff (points)` = quantile(abs(diff), 0.9),
    `Mean diff (points)` = mean(diff),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(pta_summary, digits = 1)

# The virtual cohorts are reconstructions, so individual cells near the PTA
# transition can differ by several points; assert on the centre and a robust
# envelope, not on the worst cell. A structural error (wrong clearance, volume,
# protein binding or dose cap) shifts whole columns by tens of points.
stopifnot(all(pta_summary$`Median abs diff (points)` < 3))
stopifnot(all(pta_summary$`90th pct abs diff (points)` < 15))
stopifnot(all(abs(pta_summary$`Mean diff (points)`) < 6))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Residual error form.** The paper states a "combined" error model fitted in
  Monolix without giving the formula. It is encoded as Monolix `combined1`
  (`SD = a + b * f`), the Monolix default combined form. It does not affect any
  of the PTA or NCA checks above, which use individual predictions.
* **Random-effect scale.** Table 2 prints CV%; variances are
  `log(1 + CV^2)`, cross-checked against the bootstrap medians printed on the
  omega (SD) scale.
* **Postnatal-age cut.** Table 2 labels the ka effect 'age < 21d' while the
  Results and Supplementary Appendix C equations write it as PNA <= 21 days.
  The equation form (<= 21 days) is used. The canonical `PNA` column is in
  months and converted to days in `model()`.
* **Postmenstrual age of older subjects.** Gestational age was recorded only
  in the infant study; the authors assigned 40 weeks to older subjects, so
  `PAGE` for a child or adult is 40 weeks plus postnatal age. With TM50 = 42.96
  weeks and a Hill coefficient of 5.06, the maturation term is about 0.98 at
  one year of age and above 0.999 from about three years.
* **FFM equation.** Supplementary Appendix A describes two FFM approaches
  (Al-Sallami/Janmahasatian with total body weight below 3 years, and the
  O'Hanlon 2023 neonate-to-adult method, capped at 95% of body weight) without
  saying which fed the final model. The Table 1 infant medians (FFM below body
  weight) point to the O'Hanlon method. Users must supply FFM directly; this
  vignette uses Janmahasatian for adults and 0.893 x weight for infants.
* **Virtual cohorts.** The paper's PK-Sim populations are not published, so
  the adult and infant cohorts here are reconstructions (see *Virtual
  cohorts*) at 200 subjects each, against 5000 per group in the paper. Only
  two of the paper's 11 age groups are reproduced; the paediatric groups
  between 2 months and 18 years would need a paediatric FFM equation whose
  constants the paper does not print.
* **Visual predictive check.** Figure 1 is a VPC against the pooled observed
  data, which is not public, so it is not reproduced.
* **Bioavailability.** All parameters are apparent oral values; no `F` is
  encoded.
